findings.title: Arbitrary foundation family can produce incorrectly sized instances
findings.body: The command selects the first Structural Foundation FamilySymbol without verifying that it represents a compatible isolated rectangular footing. It then looks up parameters by the localized names "Length" and "Width" and silently continues when either parameter is absent or read-only. A wall foundation, pile, circular footing, localized family, or otherwise incompatible symbol can therefore be duplicated and placed at its default dimensions while the command reports success. Select or require a supported family type and validate both writable dimension parameters before placing any instances.

findings.title: Non-rectangular and segmented outlines are converted to wrong footing dimensions
findings.body: Every closed polyline with at least four edges is treated as a rectangular foundation, but length and width are derived from only the four longest individual segments. This accepts polygons that are not rectangles and miscalculates otherwise rectangular outlines containing intermediate collinear vertices. For example, splitting one side of a 10-by-5 rectangle creates edge lengths 10, 5, 5, 5, 5 and produces a length of 7.5. The parser should first normalize collinear segments and validate a four-corner rectangular outline, then derive dimensions and orientation from its paired sides.

findings.title: Rolled-back transaction can be reported as successful
findings.body: Transaction.Commit() returns a TransactionStatus, including RolledBack, but the return value is ignored. Revit failure handling can roll back a commit without this code reaching the exception handler, after which the command displays that all foundations were created and returns Result.Succeeded. Check that Commit() returns TransactionStatus.Committed before reporting success.
